extracted.intended_audience: MathOverflow users (new and existing contributors; research mathematicians participating in the Q&A)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for asking, answering, and otherwise participating on the MathOverflow Q&A site (community standards, content quality, moderation, and reputation mechanics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Q&A model
rubrics_metrics.description: "Anybody can ask a question"; "Anybody can answer"; "The best answers are voted up and rise to the top."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the core participatory model: open question asking and answering, with community voting as the primary mechanism for surfacing high-quality answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: What types of questions should I avoid asking?
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading on the Help Center: "What types of questions should I avoid asking?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates there are categories of off-topic/unsuitable questions; users should consult the linked guidance to learn which question types are inappropriate for MathOverflow (e.g., not research-level, opinion-based, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed or on hold
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "What does it mean if a question is 'closed' or 'on hold'?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure/on-hold is a moderation action signaling a question is currently unsuitable for answers; it can often be improved by editing and potentially reopened. See linked article for specific close reasons and remediation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topicality — what topics can I ask about here?
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "What topics can I ask about here?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathOverflow has a scope of acceptable topics (primarily research-level mathematics); users should verify topicality before posting by consulting this guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be nice (behavior expected of users)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline: "Be nice." and related Help Center links: "What kind of behavior is expected of users?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civility and respectful interaction are required. See the code-of-conduct-style guidance for examples of acceptable/unacceptable behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to not be a spammer
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "How to not be a spammer"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates explicit anti-spam rules and expectations (avoid promotional content, irrelevant links, and patterns that trigger spam flags). Consult the linked article for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to write a good answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "How do I write a good answer?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance expected to include norms for answer quality: be clear, correct, sufficiently detailed, and targeted to the question; support claims with explanation or references where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "How to reference material written by others"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers and posts should properly cite sources and attribute ideas/quotations to avoid plagiarism; use links and bibliographic information as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted answer semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "What does it mean when an answer is 'accepted'?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is the asker's indication that an answer solved their problem; acceptance is separate from community voting and signals resolution from the asker's perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-answer policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "Can I answer my own question?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-answering is permitted; there are norms/rules about accepting your own answer and about posting an answer that substantially helps others. See linked guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings under "Reputation & Moderation": "Who are the site moderators, and what is their role here?"; "Why is voting important?"; "What is reputation? How do I earn (and lose) it?"; "Why do I have a reputation change on my reputation page that says 'serial upvoting/downvoting reversed'?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting is the primary mechanism for evaluating content and awarding reputation; reputation unlocks privileges. Moderators and automated systems (e.g., serial-vote reversal) maintain integrity. Consult the linked pages for how actions affect reputation and the role of moderators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate limits and automatic bans
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings: "Why are questions no longer being accepted from my account?" and "Why are answers no longer being accepted from my account?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system enforces rate limits and quality-based bans on asking/answering when contributions are repeatedly low-quality; users should follow guidance to improve posts to lift restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag wiki excerpt guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "What should a tag wiki excerpt contain?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag excerpts should succinctly describe the tag’s usage and help users apply tags correctly; see the Help Center article for format and length expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderators and privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings: "Who are the site moderators, and what is their role here?" and "Privileges — View a full list of privileges you can earn"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains moderator responsibilities and that certain moderation and site functions are unlocked by earning reputation; see privilege list for reputation thresholds and actions associated with each privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "Badges — View a full list of badges you can earn"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badges reward certain behaviors and milestones; consult the badge list for specific award criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding topics and using site features
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading: "How do I find topics I'm interested in?" and the promotion to "Take the 2-minute tour"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic site-use guidance to help new users find questions/tags of interest and quickly learn how the site works via the tour; useful for producing better questions/answers by understanding norms and navigation.
